title: Sprint-aligned build pipeline, RC flagging, and changelog automation
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Our current weekly release process is brittle for sprint-aligned feature windows. RC tagging often lags the build pipeline, changelog generation is manual and fragmented across PRs, and LTS promotion lacks clear gating signals. This causes last-minute hotfix churn and unclear upgrade guidance for customers.

Objective: Build a sprint-aligned CI pipeline that produces deterministic weekly build artifacts, automatically flags RC candidates based on gating criteria, and generates a consolidated changelog and release notes draft. The system should support stable LTS channels and provide deterministic upgrade tooling (upgrade-assistant config + migration notes) to reduce rollback rate.

Scope:
- CI pipeline changes (build slice tagging, artifact immutability)
- RC candidate detector (tests, regressions, perf check signals)
- Changelog automation (PR parsing + manual annotations)
- LTS promotion playbook + automation hooks for rolling upgrades
- Integrations with Console release dashboard and internal runbook links
acceptance_criteria:
1) CI produces a uniquely versioned weekly artifact (YYYY.MM.WW) and stores metadata to S3 and release-dashboard.
2) RC candidates are auto-flagged when pass criteria: e2e smoke, per-component integration, no new SLO regressions >3% in last 24h, and security scans green.
3) A draft release notes markdown is auto-generated combining PR bodies, cherry-picks, and manual highlights; available as a GitHub draft PR labeled 'release-draft'.
4) LTS promotion job can be triggered with a single API call that performs pre-promotion checks and schedules staged rollouts.
5) All changes covered by unit/integration tests and a runbook entry created in Confluence.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
- Introduce a 'slice' sharding strategy in build pipeline that produces weekly-YYYYMM artifacts to keep builds idempotent across branch merges.
- Implement an RC-Detector Lambda (initial PoC) that consumes CI event stream and evaluates gating rules. Rules codified in YAML so product/QA can adjust thresholds without code changes.
- Use semantic tags in PRs (#release-note: fix, #release-note: doc, #skip-changelog) to aid changelog generator. Default behavior: pull PR title + body + author + labels.
- Changelog generator runs on merge to main and on RC flag events; it opens a GitHub draft PR with generated MD and a checklist for PM to complete.
- LTS promotion service will orchestrate a canary schedule (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and call the upgrade-assistant to verify customer-specific config knobs.

Tech trade-offs considered:
- Option A (heavy CI): add more gating within CI itself; pros: single source of truth, cons: increases CI time and developer wait.
- Option B (event-driven detector + async validation): pros: faster merge feedback, decouples slow checks; cons: more moving parts and eventual consistency.
We chose Option B for pragmatic velocity and to reduce developer-perceived flakiness while keeping strong telemetry to detect drift.
automation_tasks:
- Add build slice versioning and artifact metadata to ci/buildkite (PR: github.com/redwood/ci/pull/4123).
- Deploy RC-Detector PoC as serverless job (repo: github.com/redwood/release-detector, branch: poC/sprint-slice).
- Implement changelog-generator microservice (repo: github.com/redwood/changelog-gen, PR: #56).
- Add semantic PR lint rule to enforce release-note tags (adept plugin).
- Create Concourse job that triggers LTS promotion API and logs outputs to release-dashboard.
runbook_updates: Create page: Confluence -> Release Playbook -> Sprint-aligned CI and RC Detector. Include: gating thresholds, rollback steps, emergency hotfix flow, postmortem template. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Sprint+CI+Playbook
changelog_policy:
- PRs must include a release-note tag.
- Default changelog pulls merged PRs since last week build.
- PMs can add 'human_highlights' in the draft GitHub PR.
- Changelog generator supports templates for runtime, console, and client SDK sections.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Canary): Run RC-Detector in shadow mode for two weeks; validate that flagged RCs match manual selections.
Phase 2 (Opt-in): Allow opt-in RC flagging on a subset of weekly builds; PMs get draft PRs automatically.
Phase 3 (Enforced): Turn on auto-flagging for non-blocking RCs and enable scheduled LTS promotion jobs with manual approval gates.
Emergency rollback: immediate rollback via 'release-cli rollback --artifact <version>' and trigger a postmortem.
migration_plan:
- Provide 'upgrade-assistant' JSON diff output for each release.
- Ship a CLI helper that lists breaking changes and migration steps (repo: github.com/redwood/upgrade-assistant, issue #22).
- For LTS promotions, include a compatibility matrix in the release notes and a list of recommended config changes.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Add metrics: rc_detector.flags_total, changelog.gen_time_seconds, lts.promotion_success_rate.
- Dashboards added to release-dashboard with per-release health and SLO regressions.
- PagerDuty: tag 'release-engineering' for failed promotions or RC Detector critical errors.

outstanding_risks:
- Test flakiness causing incorrect RC flags.
- Edge cases for backported patches on LTS channels requiring special changelog handling.
- Complexity in rollback automation for cross-region deployments.
next_steps:
1) Finish changelog PR and get PM template signoff (owner: Sofia Patel).
2) Address KMS requirement from security ticket (ENG-85211).
3) Harden smoke tests used by RC-Detector (owner: QA team).
4) Create a small internal beta with three customers for LTS promotion flow.
customer_impact_summary: Improvements reduce customer upgrade friction by providing clearer release notes and deterministic artifacts; short-term risk of noisy RC flagging for internal teams until flakiness is resolved.
